subject.title: fix(models): shape unreleased Claude ids with the newest known contract

question: Should Anthropic and Claude CLI IDs from generations newer than OpenClaw knows be optimistically shaped as the latest known Claude contract, or remain unavailable until provider capability/contract evidence is available?
rationale: The patch is mechanically focused, but it changes the product failure mode for arbitrary future provider contracts; tests can validate the mapping logic but cannot establish that an unreleased API contract is compatible.

options.title: Retain explicit unknown-contract handling
options.body: Keep newer unknown generations hidden or unsupported until a provider capability contract or targeted model update establishes their request shape.

options.title: Accept latest-contract forward compatibility
options.body: Merge the mapping as an intentional best-effort policy, accepting that a future Anthropic generation may require a follow-up when its contract diverges.

options.title: Define capability-driven routing first
options.body: Resolve the broader catalog issue with a durable capability-to-contract mechanism, then make every model-entry path use that shared provider-owned policy.

recommendation.title: Retain explicit unknown-contract handling
recommendation.body: Keep newer unknown generations hidden or unsupported until a provider capability contract or targeted model update establishes their request shape.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and the canonical issue history connect this contributor most directly to the Anthropic discovery and contract boundary.
